c.tagline: Silver-sand beaches, a colonial arcade old town, and the ferry to volcanic Weizhou Island.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are metered; Didi ride-hailing is widely used and often easier than hailing on the street.

emergency.note: 110 reaches the police, 120 an ambulance and 119 the fire brigade.

avoid.reason: Confirm seafood prices in writing before ordering near Silver Beach and the old town — overcharging tourists is the main complaint, along with pushy Weizhou Island tour touts.

hood_desc: The resort strip along Beihai's famous Silver Beach (Yintan) in Yinhai District, lined with big seaside hotels, promenades and fine white sand; best for beachgoers who want to stay steps from the water.
Beihai's atmospheric 19th-century old street, a 1.4-km run of Chinese-Western 'qilou' arcade houses full of pearl shops, cafes and snack stalls; best for history, photos and strolling.
The commercial heart around Beibuwan Square, with malls, department stores, restaurants and the best transit links; a convenient central base for first-timers.
A causeway-linked fishing harbour famous for its open-air seafood restaurants and night market; best for a lively evening of fresh Beibu Gulf catch.
China's largest volcanic island, an hour by ferry, with sea cliffs, a Catholic church, coral and quiet guesthouses; best for a slow overnight escape from the city.

water.note: Drink bottled or boiled water, as locals do.

transit.hours: City buses run roughly 6:00 AM to 10:00 PM; Didi and taxis cover later hours.
transit.note: Beihai has no metro; public transport is city buses, plentiful taxis and Didi ride-hailing, plus passenger ferries from the International Passenger Terminal to Weizhou Island.
transit.pay: City bus fares are a flat CNY 1-2 paid by mobile QR (WeChat/Alipay), transit card or exact cash; most locals pay by phone.

food.name: Beibu Gulf steamed seafood
food.desc: Prawns, blue crab, razor clams and mantis shrimp landed that morning and simply steamed or blanched, dipped in soy, ginger and vinegar.

places.name: Waisha Seafood Island
places.area: Waisha Island, north of the old town
places.note: Causeway island packed with seafood halls; pick live shellfish from tanks and have it cooked to order.

places.name: Qiaogang fishing port food street
places.note: Vietnamese-Chinese returnee port where boats unload; cheapest and freshest seafood in Beihai.

places.name: Nanzhu seafood market
places.note: Buy your own catch by weight and pay a nearby kitchen a small fee to cook it.

food.name: Charcoal-grilled oysters
food.desc: Fat Beibu Gulf oysters grilled in the half shell over charcoal with garlic, chilli and vermicelli; ordered by the dozen with cold beer.

places.name: Qiaogang night barbecue street
places.note: Rows of open-air grills that run past midnight; the local benchmark for garlic oysters.

places.name: Waisha Seafood Island
places.note: Grill stalls along the water charge little per oyster and shuck them in front of you.

places.name: Silver Beach food stalls
places.note: Evening stalls behind the beach grill oysters and scallops for sunset crowds.

food.name: Shachongchong (sand worm)
food.desc: Beihai's oddest delicacy: peanut worm dug from tidal flats, dried and served as a crisp fried snack, in clear soup or set into a savoury jelly.

places.name: Waisha Seafood Island
places.note: Restaurants here do the classic sand-worm and radish soup as well as fried versions.

places.name: Beihai Old Street
places.note: Arcaded colonial street with shops selling dried sand worm and small kitchens cooking it.

places.name: Nanzhu seafood market
places.note: Best place to see and buy the dried worms; vendors explain grades and prices.

food.name: Beihai seafood rice noodles
food.desc: Thin rice noodles in a clear pork-bone and dried-shrimp broth topped with sliced pork, tofu puffs, pickled mustard greens and often fresh crab.

places.name: Qiaogang food street
places.note: Famous for its Vietnamese-influenced noodle shops open from early morning.

places.name: Beihai Old Street
places.note: Small family noodle counters along the heritage street, busiest at breakfast.

places.name: Waisha Seafood Island
places.note: Crab and seafood noodle stalls that use the morning catch in the broth.

food.name: Beihai fish balls and fish cake
food.desc: Hand-beaten mackerel or eel paste shaped into springy balls or fried cakes, eaten in soup, skewered from a stall or added to noodles.

places.name: Beihai Old Street
places.note: Snack stalls beat and fry the paste on the spot; eat them hot from the pan.

places.name: Nanzhu seafood market
places.note: Market makers sell fish balls by weight, a local staple for home cooking.

places.name: Qiaogang food street
places.note: Noodle shops add house-made fish cake and fish balls to seafood bowls.

food.name: Sugarcane juice
food.desc: Guangxi grows much of China's sugarcane, and pressed-to-order cane juice, served cold and sometimes with lemon, is the standard hot-weather drink.

places.name: Beihai Old Street
places.note: Presses set up along the arcade all afternoon; cheap and served over ice.

places.name: Nanzhu seafood market
places.note: Market juice carts sell cane, coconut and mango by the cup at local prices.

places.name: Silver Beach promenade
places.note: Beachfront stands sell cane juice and coconut water beside the sand.

food.name: Iced Liquan beer
food.desc: Guangxi's own light lager, drunk very cold straight from the crate; the automatic partner for grilled oysters and a table of steamed shellfish.

places.name: Qiaogang night barbecue street
places.note: Crates of beer arrive at the table with the grill order; the classic Beihai night out.

landmarks: Silver Beach (Yintan)
Stretching over ten kilometers of powdery quartz sand famed for glittering silver in sunlight, this is China's most celebrated tropical beach and Beihai's signature attraction.
Beihai Old Street (Zhuhai Road)
A 1.4-kilometer strip of arcaded colonial-era shophouses blending Chinese and European styles, its weathered facades, cafes and pearl shops evoke the port's treaty-era heyday.
Weizhou Catholic Church (Shengtang Church)
Built by French missionaries in the 1880s from coral stone and volcanic rock, this Gothic country church rises improbably above Weizhou Island's banana plantations.
Crocodile Mountain Scenic Area
Weizhou's national geopark showcases lava cliffs, sea-eroded caves and a clifftop lighthouse, where boardwalks trace the raw volcanic coastline pounded by turquoise surf.
Guantouling National Forest Park
A pine-cloaked coastal headland west of town whose trails and pavilions deliver panoramic views over fishing fleets and some of Beihai's most romantic sunsets.
Jinhaiwan Mangrove Ecological Zone
Boardwalks wind through protected tidal mangroves alive with egrets, fiddler crabs and mudskippers, paired with folk performances celebrating the local Dan fishing culture.
Beihai Underwater World
One of China's larger aquariums plunges visitors into tunnels beneath sharks, rays and Gulf of Tonkin marine life, a favorite family stop near Haibin Park.
Beibu Gulf Square
The city's ceremonial heart is crowned by the soaring Pearl of the South sculpture, glowing at night as locals gather for music and evening strolls.
Haibin Park (Beihai Seaside Park)
A breezy waterfront park of palms, sculptures and promenades where locals fly kites at dusk, offering easygoing sea views without leaving the city center.
Yunnan Road Market
A bustling downtown market street where Beihai's famous South Sea pearls are traded alongside fresh and dried seafood, glassware and everyday goods.

train.note: Beihai has no international trains. High-speed services from Beihai Railway Station reach Nanning in about 90 minutes and continue to Guilin, Guangzhou and Kunming, and there are direct through trains to Beijing and Shanghai. If you are heading to Vietnam, take the train to Nanning first - the Nanning-Hanoi international service and the Youyi Guan border crossing both start there. Book on 12306 with your passport; summer weekends and the Weizhou Island season fill trains quickly.

bus.note: No scheduled international coaches leave Beihai. Long-distance buses use the terminals on Beihai Guangdong Road, being replaced by a large new terminal about 5 km from the centre; there are around a dozen daily services from Nanning's Langdong Long-Distance Bus Station (roughly 3.5 hours), overnight coaches from Guilin and Liuzhou via Nanning, and services from Shenzhen for about ¥200. Tickets are sold at terminal counters and on Chinese apps; for Vietnam you must change to a cross-border coach in Nanning.

intl.to: Weizhou Island (China) - fast catamarans from Beihai International Passenger Port
intl.op: Beihai-Weizhou Island fast ferry services (tickets via Ctrip)

intl.to: Haikou (China, Hainan) - overnight Ro-Ro sailing from Beihai port

ferry.note: Beihai is one of the few mainland cities where the boat is the main attraction: fast ferries run from the International Passenger Port out to volcanic Weizhou Island in a little over an hour, and a vehicle ferry crosses the Gulf of Tonkin to Haikou on Hainan in about 11 hours for roughly ¥67-400 depending on whether you take a seat or a berth. Weizhou sailings are capped by a daily visitor quota and sell out days ahead in summer, and both routes are cancelled outright in rough weather or when a typhoon is forecast. The Haikou boat is a Ro-Ro ship that also carries cars and motorbikes, so book vehicle space well in advance and confirm the sailing is still running before you travel.
